question: Students about to sit a maths test were told a racing heart can help performance. What happened to their scores?
answer: They rose. Jamieson and colleagues told some students preparing for the GRE, the American graduate entrance exam, that arousal during a test can improve performance. They scored higher on the maths section in the laboratory, and later in the real exam. Their hearts still pounded; what changed was what the pounding meant.
move: Read a racing heart as fuel before reading it as fear.
ask: Before my next nerve-racking moment, could I treat the pounding heart as my body getting ready?
source: Jamieson and colleagues, J. Experimental Social Psychology, 2010
reference: Jamieson, Mendes, Blackstock and Schmader, Turning the knots in your stomach into bows: Reappraising arousal improves performance on the GRE, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 2010
